School education will be split into three main levels – primary (nursery to class 4), secondary education (classes 5 to 8), and senior secondary education (classes 9 to 12) – Chief Minister Revanth Reddy said on November 11 following a review meeting of the education department. Revanth Reddy also handles the education portfolio. The CM said that under the new system, students must be trained to have a command over language and communication skills by the time they complete class 12. He expressed concern over students discontinuing their education after class 10, with dropouts consisting predominantly of girls, and children from Dalit, tribal, and minority communities. He noted that dropout rates are significantly lower in government-run institutions such as Kendriya Vidyalayas, Navodaya Vidyalayas, and Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas, which offer continuous education up to class 12. He also said Phase I of the Musi River rejuvenation project would begin soon, seeking support for the government’s plans. The lake, restored by the Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA), has been expanded to around 30 acres. More than 30,000 truckloads of silt, construction debris, plastic and other waste, including biomedical waste, were removed during the work. Its depth has increased from 0.6 metres to 4.6 metres, while its water storage capacity has risen eightfold to 370 million litres, according to HYDRAA Commissioner A V Ranganath. The restored lake has a 1.6-km walking track, an open gym, a children’s play area, landscaped gardens and seating facilities. HYDRAA also reconstructed three inlets and an outlet to improve rainwater flow and diverted sewage through a 1,200-mm pipeline to prevent wastewater from entering the lake.
